newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds creep higher, await payrolls.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds creep higher, await payrolls.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities inched their way into positive territory in late afternoon trade on Thursday, ahead of Friday's key economic data, mortgage experts said.
Fixed-rate pass-through yield spreads were largely on par with Treasuries amid a quiet trading session.
Market participants mostly stayed on the sidelines, watching a flurry of news headlines about rumors of a nearing U.S. budget deal, traders said.
"All the cards are on the table today," said one trader at an investment bank in New York.
"Everyone is keeping an eye on the newswires and basically it's just your headline trading," he said. "My feedback from retailers is that very little is going on," he added.
By late afternoon, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5-percent paper was up 7/32 at 99-12/32, yielding 92 basis points over the five-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac issues were 6/32 higher, at 99-13/32 and 99-18/32, respectively.
Five-year Treasuries were up 5/32 at 6.54 percent, and 10-year notes were up 10/32 at 6.67 percent.
Market players said Friday's employment report should give mortgage-backeds some general direction.
"We're waiting on the sidelines for tomorrow's unemployment for some concrete evidence as to where ... thing's are going," one trader said.
On average, 22 economists forecast the April unemployment figure to hold steady at 5.2 percent, while the headline payrolls figure was seen rising 211,000 from a 175,000 gain in March.
